summary: Improvement remains strategically coherent and the codified priority order is still correct. Priority refresh review found TOP_PRIORITIES.md current: P1 remains the dominant bottleneck because the canonical TDE-first improvement substrate is still not explicitly defined, P2 remains unstarted with interim-copy drift still the live distribution mode, and P3 now has its first fully closed proof case after IMP-ERR-20260315-ARCHIVED-REPO-MISUSE-01 was formally closed in TDE on 2026-03-17. That is genuine progress, but it has not yet been converted into the minimum product-side improvement interface across active products. The four Jobs Review signals remain a useful stress-test surface waiting for P1 substrate definition and canonical routing.
materialChanges: IMP-ERR-20260315-ARCHIVED-REPO-MISUSE-01 is now formally closed in TDE (closure_id CLOSE-IMP-ERR-20260315-ARCHIVED-REPO-MISUSE-01-20260317-003605-532136). This completes the first end-to-end incident-to-improvement conversion cycle and upgrades P3 from partial progress to one verified proof case.
TOP_PRIORITIES.md remains aligned with the full product stack and current execution reality. No priority reorder or wording change was required in this run.

The four Jobs Review signals (OPS-2026-066 through OPS-2026-069) remain present in canonical TDE Inbox, which strengthens the case for P1 but does not yet constitute a defined improvement substrate or deployed minimum interface.
No new execution evidence appeared for P2 pinned-lane delivery into PXS. Interim-copy / drift exposure remains unchanged.

topPriorities.title: Converge improvement execution into one canonical TDE-first system of record
topPriorities.why: Improvement still lacks an explicitly defined canonical substrate in TDE terms (queue ID, linkage rules, intake format). Without that, signals can enter TDE, but the product still does not have one deliberate, reusable execution path for improvement work.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Strategic direction remains clear. Jobs Review signals are now in canonical TDE Inbox, but the substrate definition itself is still missing.
topPriorities.nextStep: Define the canonical improvement execution substrate in TDE terms (queue ID, linkage rules, intake format); update improvement runbooks to use it; then route the current Jobs Review signals through that substrate as first validation cases.

topPriorities.title: Ship A-005 into PXS through a pinned lane with version truth, rollback, and verification semantics
topPriorities.why: Improvement distribution is still not living through a pinned-lane path with machine-checkable installed-version truth. Interim-copy drift remains the active exposure.
topPriorities.currentStatus: No new delivery evidence. No pinned-lane implementation or verification movement since the prior report.
topPriorities.nextStep: Implement the pinned lane as an operational path with machine-checkable installed-version truth, explicit rollback behavior, and a verification pass that closes the interim-drift gap.

topPriorities.title: Roll out the minimum improvement interface across active products, starting with mandatory incident-to-improvement conversion
topPriorities.why: The first full proof case now exists, which makes the interface ready to formalize from evidence rather than theory. But the interface has not yet been specified and deployed across products.
topPriorities.currentStatus: One complete proof case exists (IMP-ERR-20260315 closed). Four additional improvement-eligible signals are present in TDE Inbox. No minimum interface spec or rollout evidence yet.
topPriorities.nextStep: Formalize the minimum product-side improvement interface (intake format, linkage rules, review cadence, mandatory conversion rule for material incidents) using IMP-ERR-20260315 as the reference pattern; then begin deployment across active products.

constraints: Improvement must remain evidence-backed and must not become a narrative-only reporting layer.
